top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is one mechanistic idea, a small molecule that brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase so the cell destroys it, realised by design (PROTACs, Crews and Deshaies) and by ligase reprogramming (thalidomide-type glues, cereblon, Handa). It is event-driven pharmacology built on molecular recognition and ternary-complex cooperativity, reproduced across many laboratories and E3 ligases, and it changes what chemists and clinicians can do. The three-name allocation and the single citation leave Ciulli and others outside and no degrader is yet approved, but the science is mature and the only shortlisted case ranked by all eight members. Base editing is next, then C-N coupling as the most mature but least novel option.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; overlapping peptide and lipid self-assembly interests with Emma Sparr (B061 supporter) are scientific proximity only
